item.title: About
item.description: Personal Information I am a postdoc at The University of British Columbia in Vancouver, Canada. My research focuses on environmental transport processes, including river turbulence, granular flows, and fluid-driven sediment transport. I am educated in multiple disciplines, with PhD training in geomorphology and hydrology, and MSc training in statistical and condensed matter physics. This interdisciplinary background has enabled me to produce unique research that blends ideas from physics and geoscience.

item.title: Teaching Experience
item.description: To date my teaching work has mainly involved teaching assistantships and course content development. Course Development During my PhD I gained a lot of experience incorporating emerging virtual technologies into university courses: Developed five laboratory assignments with solutions and introductory materials for a fourth year undergraduate Fluvial Geomorphology course. Produced a 45min geomorphology ``Virtual Field Trip" video documentary involving a tour of the UBC Research Forest and pedagogical explanations of various features.
